description:
Change the world. Love your job. 
Texas Instruments (TI) is looking for an experienced Facilities Controls Enginee r to join our team to support our PLC/SCADA development. As a Facilities Engineer at TI, you'll be directly responsible for building utility systems in support of a semiconductor wafer fab. TI Facilities operates over 150 different utility systems that include chemicals, gasses, variety of electrical systems, water systems, HVAC, waste, vacuum, and controls. These systems are designed to run 24 hours a day, 365 days a year without interruption, creating a state of the art manufacturing environment. Facilities works closely with TI's manufacturing team to understand how the utility systems impact the process as well as how to reduce consumption.

 Responsibilities include: 
 Design, implement, and troubleshoot controls systems and instrumentation, including a variety of flow, pressure, temperature, level, pH, and water quality monitoring equipment
 Program and troubleshoot programmable logic controllers (PLCs), including PLC hardware (including I/O interface    modules) and PLC programming software
 Program and troubleshoot Supervisory Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) systems for monitoring facility systems
 Design, implement, and troubleshoot a secure and reliable industrial network to support communication between devices on the network (e.g. peer communication between PLCs and PLC communication with SCADA drivers)
 Assist with development and execution of the controls-related scope in facility expansion and sustaining projects (e.g. Process and Instrumentation Diagrams, Sequence of Operations, I/O lists, panel drawings, instrumentations lists, etc.)
 Understand industrial equipment & processes, their operating parameters, and make decisions (with engineering support) to improve or maintain the associated controls and instrumentation hardware & software
 Provide technical controls support for the 24-hour operations team
 Ensure projects and systems are compliant with applicable codes (e.g. National Electric Code, International Fire Code, etc.)
 Influence supplier performance via management and audits of work performed in the field
 Develop relationships and communicate with engineers across disciplines and at other TI sites to foster best practice sharing and communication 
  
 Texas Instruments will not sponsor job applicants for visas or work authorization for this position. 


 Minimum Requirements: 
 Bachelor’s degree in engineering 
 5+ years of relevant engineering experience with industrial controls and instrumentation systems
 
 Preferred Qualifications: 
 Experience with PLCs and/or SCADA systems
 Experience in application of controls and instrumentation for process systems (process cooling water, hot water, air systems, exhaust, chem/gas distribution, etc.)
 Proven Experience with Siemens, Rockwell Automation/Allen Bradley, or WAGO PLCs (PLC hardware and software)
 Proven Experience programming PLCs using Control narratives or sequence of Operations (Siemens, Rockwell Automation/Allen Bradley, or WAGO PLCs
 Experience with development or delivery of turnkey Wonderware/Operation Management Interface (OMI) SCADA systems 
 Experience in industrial network design, configuration, installation, maintenance, security strategies, troubleshooting, etc. 
 Basic understanding of PID loop tuning
 Able to terminate instrumentation to a controller and perform calibration through the program interface
 Able to troubleshoot alarms, field instrumentation, pneumatic and electric control valves, variable speed drives and motor starters
 Experience managing multi-discipline projects
 Able to respond quickly to potentially critical situations, perform rapid, accurate assessments, identify causes of failures, determine appropriate corrective actions, and implement these corrections promptly to mitigate the effects of system upsets
 Proficient with PC hardware and windows-based applications 
 
 
 
 Why TI? 
 

 
 
 Engineer your future. We empower our employees to truly own their career and development. Come collaborate with some of the smartest people in the world to shape the future of electronics.

 We're different by design. Diverse backgrounds and perspectives are what push innovation forward and what make TI stronger. We value each and every voice, and look forward to hearing yours.  Meet the people of TI 

 Benefits that benefit you. We offer competitive pay and benefits designed to help you and your family live your best life. Your well-being is important to us. Please find our country-specific benefits here 

 
 

 
 

 

 
 

 
 About Texas Instruments 
 

 
 Texas Instruments Incorporated (Nasdaq: TXN) is a global semiconductor company that designs, manufactures and sells analog and embedded processing chips for markets such as industrial, automotive, data center, personal electronics and communications equipment. At our core, we have a passion to create a better world by making electronics more affordable through semiconductors. This passion is alive today as each generation of innovation builds upon the last to make our technology more reliable, more affordable and lower power, making it possible for semiconductors to go into electronics everywhere. Learn more at  TI.com .
 

 
 

 

 
 
 Texas Instruments is an equal opportunity employer and supports a diverse, inclusive work environment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, disability, genetic information, national origin, gender, gender identity and expression, age, sexual orientation, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local laws.
 

 
 

 

 
 If you are interested in this position, please apply to this requisition.
